'''Paul Meier''' (July 24, 1924 – August 7, 2011)<ref name=hevesi>{{citation |last=Hevesi |first=Dennis|title=Paul Meier, Statistician Who Revolutionized Medical Trials, Dies at 87 | newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |date=August 12, 2011 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2011/08/13/health/13meier.html}}</ref> was a [[statistician]] who promoted the use of [[random assignment|randomized trials]] in medicine.<ref name=wpbrown>{{cite news | title = Paul Meier, biostatistician and co-inventor of a famous graph, dies at 87 | url = https://www.washingtonpost.com/local/obituaries/paul-meier-biostatistician-and-co-inventor-of-a-famous-graph-dies-at-87/2011/08/09/gIQAfHBH7I_story.html | author = David Brown | date = August 10, 2011 | newspaper = [[Washington Post]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | title = Paul Meier, Obituary | url = https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/obituaries/medicine-obituaries/8804883/Paul-Meier.html | date = October 2, 2011 | publisher = [[The Daily Telegraph]]}}</ref>

Meier is known for introducing, with [[Edward L. Kaplan]], the [[Kaplan–Meier estimator]],<ref>Kaplan, E. L.; Meier, P.: Nonparametric estimation from incomplete observations. ''J. Amer. Statist. Assn.'' '''53''':457–481, 1958. {{JSTOR|2281868}}</ref><ref>Kaplan, E.L. in a retrospective on the seminal paper in "This week's citation classic". ''Current Contents'' '''24''', 14 (1983).[http://www.garfield.library.upenn.edu/classics1983/A1983QS51100001.pdf Available from UPenn as PDF.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160412025025/http://garfield.library.upenn.edu/classics1983/A1983QS51100001.pdf |date=2016-04-12 }}</ref> a [[nonparametric estimator]] of [[survival function]]s that accounts for changes in sample size over time.<ref>{{citation | journal = [[Clinical Trials (journal)|Clinical Trials]] | year = 2004 | volume = 1 | issue = 1 | pages = 131–138 | url = http://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/bin/m/b/meier.pdf | title = A conversation with Paul Meier | author = Harry M Marks | doi = 10.1191/1740774504cn011xx | pmid = 16281468 | citeseerx = 10.1.1.575.5895 | s2cid = 71816703 | access-date = 2011-08-14 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110206062213/http://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/bin/m/b/meier.pdf | archive-date = 2011-02-06 | url-status = dead }}</ref>

Meier's 1957 evaluation of polio vaccine practices published in ''Science'' has been described as influential, and the Kaplan–Meier method is thought to have indirectly extended tens of thousands of lives.<ref name=wpbrown/>
